 The Mizuho Blue Challenge – The Kallang Football Series Singapore kicks off tomorrow (13 November) with the Lions taking on 33rd-ranked Paraguay at the National Stadium.
 This marks the team’s first return to the iconic venue since their 1–0 triumph over Bangladesh in March this year, which capped an unbeaten Asian Football Confederation (AFC) Asian Cup Saudi Arabia 2027 Qualifying campaign.
 Despite the AFC’s confirmation earlier this month that the Asian Cup had been postponed to December 2027, Head Coach Gavin Lee insists that his team remain fully focused on the matches ahead.
 “The postponement gives us a longer runway to prepare for the Asian Cup, but it is now our responsibility to make the most of the additional time and opportunities we have. We need to maximise every international window, continue improving as a team and ensure that we arrive at the tournament as the best versions of ourselves.
 “And that process starts with these two matches, beginning with Paraguay tomorrow,” Lee said.
 Paraguay will provide a stern test for Lee’s charges, with the South American side boasting the likes of Premier League players Julio Enciso and Diego Gomez, as well as former Newcastle United winger Miguel Almiron.
 However, Lee believes the opportunity to take on World Cup opposition is one that his players should embrace.
 “We are relishing the opportunity to test ourselves against a team of Paraguay’s calibre. We know they will put us under pressure and overload us in many areas of the pitch, but that is exactly the kind of challenge we need.
 “It will require us to be comfortable with being uncomfortable, remain calm under pressure and stay consistent in our actions throughout the match,” he added.
 The match is set to kick off at 8pm with tickets still available at the link here .
